subject: Publisher partnership: distribution & weights bundling discussion
messages:
From: Elena Popov <elena@openweightslabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Distribution partnership: OpenWeights model bundles and hosting

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. OpenWeights Labs is exploring a lightweight distribution arrangement for our latest open foundation model (OWL-3-small) so ISV/platform partners like Redwood can offer a pre-bundled, provenance-verified weights package to end customers.

High-level asks from our side:
- Redwood to host a non-modifiable bundle (quantized + provenance file) for Dedicated and Private deployments (customer-facing product).
- Attribution and model-card display in the UI.
- No downstream resale of raw weights; permissive use for inference by Redwood customers.
- Revenue share or referral credits for commercial deployments.

We attached a short draft that outlines the bundle and suggested clauses (OW-Distribution-Draft-v1.docx). We can also provide an S3 staging bucket and signed checksum files.

Would love to align on guardrails (what counts as "redistribution" vs inference), support expectations, and whether Redwood needs special license language for Private/on-prem installs.

Best,
Elena
Head of Partnerships, OpenWeights Labs
--
Attachments: OW-Distribution-Draft-v1.docx, s3-access-instructions.txt

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Popov <elena@openweightslabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Distribution partnership: OpenWeights model bundles and hosting

Elena — thanks for the note and the draft, appreciated. Looping in Laura (partnerships) and Karthik (legal/terms) so we can triage.

Initial quick thoughts:
- We can surface a pre-bundled model in Redwood Console and make the weights available to Dedicated and Private customers, but legal needs clarity on "non-modifiable" (does that allow quantization for runtime?).
- For Private/on‑prem, customers typically host locally; we need to confirm what the publisher requires for direct hosting vs Redwood-hosted bundle.
- We should define an allowed-subset: inference-only, no re-export of raw parameter files, fingerprint verification on startup, and clear product UI attribution.

Next steps proposal:
1) Karthik & Laura review the draft and propose redlines by EOD Thu.
2) Quick sync next week with your legal/ops to cover S3 access, checksums, and simple SLA for support.

If useful, I can sketch a one-pager with the allowed behaviors and technical requirements.

Thanks — Sergio
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
--
Sent from Redwood mailbox

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: redlines for OWL distribution draft

Folks — I reviewed OW-Distribution-Draft-v1.docx and prepared a short list of negotiation points for commercial/legal:

1) Definition tidy-up:
   - "Distribution" should be explicitly "making weights available for download"; we will accept inference-only bundling where Redwood serves quantized runtime artifacts and a signed provenance file.
2) Quantization & derivatives:
   - Allow quantization for runtime performance (Redwood will produce runtime artifacts) provided the original raw FP32 weights are never redistributed.
3) Sublicense & customer installs:
   - For Private deployments, customer may host the bundle locally under their contract; Redwood must not grant third-party sublicenses beyond the customer's use.
4) Security & provenance:
   - Require signed checksums and a model fingerprint API we can call on load.
5) Support & SLAs:
   - Define a triage window (48 business hours) for model regressions that are attributable to the publisher-provided bundle; define optional paid priority support.
6) IP & indemnity:
   - Keep publisher indemnity for IP claims but limit Redwood liability to our delivery of the runtime.

I'll convert this to inline redlines on the doc and circulate. Also flagged a potential sticky point: publishing the bundle to our marketplace could trigger export/compliance clauses depending on country of use (we should ask OWL for a minimal compliance statement).

—Karthik
Senior Counsel (approx.), Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Li <marcus.li@openweightslabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-14T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Distribution partnership: OpenWeights model bundles and hosting

Thanks for the quick review. A few clarifications from our side after talking to OW Legal:
- "Non-modifiable" was shorthand — we expect runtime quantization/optimizations to be fine; we just don't want wholesale re-sharing of the original checkpoint.
- We'll provide signed checksums and a provenance.json with training-data provenance notes (high-level).
- Regarding Private installs: we are OK with customers self-hosting under the customer's contract; OWL won't grant additional sublicenses to third parties.
- Revenue share: open to a referral credit model (one-time credit per paid customer) rather than a percent take — simplifies accounting.

I've attached a one-page NDA-exec summary (NDA-Exec-Summary.pdf) and our S3 access instructions. If you can confirm the compliance checklist items (country restrictions + intended use cases), we can prepare a legal-friendly draft for redlines.

Can we schedule a 30-min call Wed 4/21 to finalize the commercial points?

Cheers,
Marcus
Ops Lead, OpenWeights Labs
--
Attachments: NDA-Exec-Summary.pdf, s3-access-instructions.txt

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Li <marcus.li@openweightslabs.com>, Elena Popov <elena@openweightslabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Distribution partnership: OpenWeights model bundles and hosting

Marcus / Elena — perfect, this is shaping up. Quick confirmation and next steps: 

- We agree to allow Redwood-side quantization and runtime artifact generation; Redwood will not redistribute raw FP32 checkpoints.
- Redwood will require signed checksums/provenance.json on every bundle; we'll add fingerprint verification on model load.
- For go-to-market, we'll build a co-branded listing in Redwood Console and propose a one-time referral credit for first paid deployment (details to be tracked in HubSpot, deal OWL-2026-042).
- Karthik will circulate a redline draft by Tue 4/20 EOD with suggested compliance language.

I'll set up the Wed 4/21 30-min call and share a calendar invite + agenda. Thanks all — excited to make this a clean, repeatable pattern for other publishers.

Sergio
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
